title: Choose the PortWatch dashboard direction
question: PortWatch watches real local listeners. Choose the visual system that will make their port, process, and project relationships easiest to operate.

options.label: Signal Interlocking
options.lineage: railway signal cabin plans and interlocking diagrams
options.thesis: Every listener reads as an occupied route with a traceable owner.
options.viewport: One open route field. Port number, process, and project sit on connected rails; a slim service strip holds scan time, search, and range filters.
options.risk: Rail colors can imply free or blocked states that the scanner does not know; every shown state must have a factual label.

raised.raise: Keep every port and owner aligned to a crisp shared grid; no hidden details or novelty animation.
Name each process and detected project at the point its route resolves.
Pair every status color with the literal status text; the scanner reports listening, not inferred availability.
Keep labels literal and action copy direct; confirmation states stay distinct from passive scan states.
Keep selection anchored to one port as the list refreshes, without inventing a history timeline.
Preserve strong single-ink contrast for dense values and never encode status by hue alone.

options.label: The Switchboard
options.thesis: A live connection board makes each local port’s owner visible at a glance.
options.viewport: A horizontal exchange panel with numbered socket rails and straight, labeled runs to the process and project directory; the search field acts as the operator’s selector.
options.risk: Ports are logical sockets, not physical cable connections; avoid implying network topology beyond the observed port-to-process relationship.

options.label: eBoy Pixorama Metropolis
options.thesis: Every process becomes a tiny inhabitant in a zoomable digital town.
options.viewport: A busy pixel city where each block can be explored to reveal process owners.
options.case: Fuses poorly: port occupancy is a precise operational lookup, and city exploration obscures the owner relationship.
options.kept: A shared pixel grid becomes exact alignment and immediate labels, without pixel art or hidden novelty.
options.risk: Dense process names become illegible if the interface is reduced to sprites.

options.label: Busytown Cross-Section
options.thesis: A continuous cutaway shows each port and the process busy behind it.
options.viewport: A wall-to-wall illustrated machine room with labeled ports and working processes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the product has no visual machine room to explore, and illustration weakens dense live inventory.
options.kept: Every real process and detected project gets a readable label at its endpoint.
options.risk: A painted scene could imply hardware or process relationships that PortWatch did not observe.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: measured color fringes in atmospheric imaging
options.thesis: Subtle color bands distinguish changing port activity.
options.viewport: A calm white observation surface with fine color fringes on active rows.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the current scanner exposes no measured activity trend or particle-like variable to visualize.
options.kept: Restrict color to explicitly reported states and label them in text.
options.risk: Soft atmospheric color can make live process state ambiguous.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.lineage: stockroom garment tags and hazard labeling
options.thesis: Literal labels and safety marks turn port actions into a tagged tool panel.
options.viewport: A high-contrast tool rail with tagged process rows and conspicuous termination controls.
options.case: Fuses poorly: quoted garment language and hazard stripes are a costume around ordinary port records.
options.kept: Use direct, literal labels on every destructive action and confirmation.
options.risk: Decorative warning marks would make routine scan data feel hazardous.

options.label: Film Cutting Bench
options.lineage: perforated film select rails and edit benches
options.thesis: A snapped rail records the listener selected for inspection.
options.viewport: A perforated horizontal strip of ports with one selected row flagged in orange.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a film timeline promises retained history that this live scanner does not provide.
options.kept: Anchor keyboard and pointer selection to one visible port row through refresh.
options.risk: A scrub rail implies that past listener states can be replayed.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.thesis: A monospace character field renders active listeners as a live text scene.
options.viewport: A dense terminal-like wall of port and process names, with live refresh in place.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the port owner must be scannable as structured data, not rendered as character art.
options.kept: Maintain high contrast and tabular alignment for process names and numeric ports.
options.risk: A monochrome grid would make the web dashboard read as a decorative terminal.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean local developer dashboard, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Search and a clear live-list table with owner details and an explicit terminate action.
canonCard.risk: Less distinctive than the chosen visual worlds; success depends on exceptional information hierarchy.
